scope: Pre-publication frozen endpoint policy, probe, CLI dispatch and four endpoint test files. No immutable remote candidate supplied yet.
conclusion: CHANGES REQUESTED for the three reproducible bounded issues below. No additional DNS/TLS/proxy/target-routing bypass identified in this review.

testing.ownedTlsFixture: Actual loopback HTTPS certificate/hostname rejection using the product agent; deliberately public fixture key; isolated ephemeral port and owned socket cleanup.
testing.independentNegativeRegressions: Two additional reviewer tests fail as expected against the frozen current implementation; the transport challenger separately reproduces the CRLF limit discrepancy.

findings.reproduction: Return a valid matching legacy initialization with MCP-Session-Id SYNTHETIC_OWNED_SESSION_DO_NOT_PRINT and serverInfo.version set to that same token; acknowledge initialized and return405 to cleanup. The token appears in the returned serverInfo.
findings.impact: A known ephemeral session value can reach CLI JSON/logs through metadata, including when cleanup is unsupported. No external token or service was used.
findings.repair: Omit or redact projected serverInfo if name or version contains the adopted session value; cover exact and embedded reflection in both fields.

findings.reproduction: One 21,181-byte CRLF SSE event, containing 7,000 comment lines and a valid modern result, returns compatible/protocolChecked=true despite MAX_EVENT_BYTES 16384.
findings.impact: Raw CRLF delimiters are charged as one byte while consuming two. The separate 65,536-byte total response cap still holds; this is not unbounded memory use or SSRF.
findings.repair: Charge the actual consumed delimiter width, including split CRLF, and add exact-boundary/plus-one cases.

findings.reproduction: A legacy initialization response containing MCP-Session-Id invalid session value reports cleanup:not-needed after format rejection. It issues zero DELETE, which is correct.
findings.impact: The client observed a possible session that it cannot safely adopt; not-needed overstates the absence of cleanup uncertainty. The analogous valid-looking-but-invalid-result path already reports unconfirmed.
findings.repair: Separate observing a session header from validating/adopting it. Preserve cleanup:unconfirmed for an unusable observed legacy session without authorizing DELETE.

positiveReview: Previously reported scoped-address gap is fixed and the translated-address comment is narrowed in this snapshot.
Raw URL admission precedes parsing and any request; no profile selection, credential read or remote state-store admission is introduced on the endpoint command path.

Every bounded A/AAAA answer is checked for its claimed family and public policy. The same selected address is returned from the request lookup with no new resolver call; no alternate target or fallback is adopted.

The private agent uses explicit certificate verification, standard hostname checking, a TLS 1.2 floor, empty proxyEnv, no cached TLS sessions and bounded socket count. The owned TLS regression passes.

Modern discovery is one request with empty client capabilities. Explicit legacy mode negotiates only the three listed 2025 revisions, sends initialized to the original endpoint and adopts a session only after a valid matching initialization result.

Notification failures still run bounded cleanup for an established session. Invalid headers or invalid initialization do not authorize DELETE. All follow-ups use the original hostname, port, path and pin.

Authentication/error/redirect bodies are not consumed or printed; redirects, discovered endpoints, interactive server requests, compressed content and unrecognized protocol branches do not trigger fallback.
Total raw bytes, headers, JSON depth/node counts, SSE event count, work time, DNS time and cleanup time remain bounded. The event-byte discrepancy is separately identified.
Report fields explicitly keep credentialsUsed/routingEnabled false, distinguish protocol check from advertised capabilities and mark projected server info unverified.
limitations: This is a bounded manual review, not an exhaustive security scan.
No external MCP server, production configuration, user credential, model API or live profile was accessed.
No full CLI CI/packaging/roadmap or final immutable publication approval is supplied by this snapshot review.
Node/system trust stores and arbitrary local translation/routing remain outside this admission policy.
